questions.question: Who has the authority to recommend to the President nominees for the members of the Supreme Court and judges of lower courts?
options: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: The Judicial and Bar Council recommends nominees for appointments to the judiciary.

questions.question: The Constitutional Convention responsible for proposing amendments or revisions to the Constitution is called by a vote of:
questions.explanation: Congress may call a constitutional convention by a two-thirds vote.

questions.question: Under the 1987 Constitution, the State is mandated to assign the highest budget priority to:
questions.explanation: The Constitution provides that education shall receive the highest budgetary priority.

questions.question: Which of the following sectors is NOT represented in the House of Representatives through the party-list system?
questions.explanation: Religious sectors are not represented under the party-list system.

questions.question: The power of the President to disapprove a bill passed by Congress is called:
questions.explanation: The President may veto bills passed by Congress.

questions.question: Due process of law means that the accused is:
options: Represented in all stages of the trial
questions.explanation: An accused person is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

questions.question: The rights of private individuals to secure themselves against unwarranted interference are called:
questions.explanation: Civil rights protect private individuals from unwarranted interference.

questions.question: What is the retirement age of civil servants in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The compulsory retirement age for civil servants is 65.

questions.question: What is the retirement age of justices in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: Members of the judiciary retire at age 70.

questions.question: Who determines the existence of probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest?
questions.explanation: Only a judge may determine probable cause for issuing a warrant.

questions.question: A member of the House of Representatives may serve for no more than how many consecutive terms?
questions.explanation: Members of the House may serve for three consecutive terms.

questions.question: An accused person has the right to:
questions.explanation: The Constitution guarantees the accused the right to be informed of the accusation.

questions.question: Which branch of government interprets the law?
questions.explanation: The Judicial branch interprets laws.

questions.question: The right to vote and participate in public affairs belongs to:
questions.explanation: Political rights allow citizens to participate in government.

questions.question: The House of Representatives is composed of representatives elected for a term of:
questions.explanation: Representatives serve for three years.

questions.question: The Senate of the Philippines is composed of how many senators?
questions.explanation: The Senate is composed of 24 senators.

questions.question: The President of the Philippines serves a term of:
questions.explanation: The President serves a six-year term.

questions.question: Who is considered the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The President is the Commander-in-Chief.

questions.question: Which government body has the power to declare war?
questions.explanation: Congress has the power to declare war.

questions.question: What is the supreme law of the land in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The 1987 Constitution is the supreme law.
